title: Customer-specific eval noise from default token-filtering inheritance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported sudden divergence between their eval harness scoring and production outputs after we rolled the sampling defaults change in runtime-1.19. Symptoms include spurious trailing tokens, extra punctuation, and mismatched structured JSON fields. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and long-term fix for customer-specific regressions caused by token-filtering and sampling-parameter inheritance during routing and model fallback paths.
impact: High — affects eval parity and customer-facing generative outputs for multiple paying customers. Some customers paused rollouts and opened formal escalations. Potential churn risk if not resolved within the next 2 weeks.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer eval prompt set (see related_links) with model variant pinned to m-xlarge-v1 on dedicated pool
2) Send batched requests through routing layer with default sampling policy (no explicit stop sequence provided),
3) Observe additional terminal punctuation and occasional extra JSON keys in outputs vs. local baseline runs where legacy sampling params are applied
4) Repeat with fallback route enabled (region fallback to m-large-v1) — output mismatch is amplified when fallback variant receives inherited filter policy.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-06 — Initial pager triage: reproductions confirmed for Acme and Nimbus. Routing layer logs show policy merge at request middleware step.

2026-03-07 — Added request-level debug flag to trace sampling param inheritance. Found that 'token_filter_profile' set on org defaults is being merged into routing fallback path without precedence checks.

2026-03-09 — Kernel scheduling team reproduced mismatch locally when prefix-caching disabled. Hypothesis: when prefix cache miss occurs, fallback model is served with merged filter that modifies decode exit heuristics.
2026-03-11 — QA verified that explicitly setting end_marker param at API client restores parity for most prompts; suggests default inheritance is the primary cause.
2026-03-13 — Security reviewed: no PII leakage observed; changes are behavioral only.
Notes: routing merge logic (policy_merge_v2) applies organziation-level token filter last, unintentionally overwriting model-variant defaults for termination heuristics.
root_cause: Policy merge semantics changed in policy_merge_v2 shipped in runtime-1.19. Organization-level 'token_filter_profile' was given higher precedence than per-model 'termination_profile' during routing and fallback. This caused fallback variants to use a more permissive exit heuristic, producing extra tokens and breaking structured outputs used by eval suites.
proposed_fix: 1) Revert precedence: ensure per-request and per-model termination profiles win over org defaults (hotfix branch runtime/1.19-hotfix-token-filter). 2) Add unit/integration tests for policy precedence in routing layer. 3) Add a migration check and a feature flag to control new merge behavior.
rollout_plan: Hotfix deploy to staging and canary (dedicated pool) — runtime/1.19-hotfix-token-filter
Run customer eval harnesses for Acme/Nimbus/OneGov against canary for 48 hours
If stable, promote to production with 10% traffic canary -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours
Notify affected customers via PM and SE with remediation steps and expected timeline
qa_checks: Run end-to-end eval harnesses (deterministic seed) for affected customers and assert token-level parity with pre-change baselines
Smoke test fallback routes with explicit and implicit termination params
Verify no regressions in latency (<+5ms p95) for canonical workloads
Confirm routing logs include explicit precedence metadata for every merged policy
postmortem_actions: 1) Revert policy_merge_v2 precedence change and ship hotfix
2) Add integration tests that include fallback model paths in CI
3) Improve customer escalation docs with recommended client-side mitigations (explicit end_marker parameter guidance),
4) Run audit across org defaults to identify customers relying on permissive token filters and proactively contact them
